answer_text:
By the independent increments property of Brownian motion,

\[
B(3)=B(1)+\bigl(B(3)-B(1)\bigr),
\]

where \(B(3)-B(1)\) is independent of \(B(1)\) and is normally distributed with mean \(0\) and variance \(3-1=2\).

Given \(B(1)=1\),

\[
B(3)\mid B(1)=1 \sim N(1,2).
\]

Therefore,

\[
P(B(3)\le 3 \mid B(1)=1)
= P\left(1 + X \le 3\right),
\]

where \(X\sim N(0,2)\). Equivalently,

\[
P(B(3)\le 3 \mid B(1)=1)
= P(X\le 2).
\]

Standardizing \(X\) by letting \(Z\sim N(0,1)\),

\[
P(X\le 2)
= P\left(Z\le \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}\right)
= P(Z\le \sqrt{2})
= \Phi(\sqrt{2}).
\]

Thus,

\[
\boxed{\Phi(\sqrt{2})}
\]

where \(\Phi\) is the standard normal cumulative distribution function.
